title: Cycle Capacity Sentinel & Skill-Rotor: automated buffer orchestration for rolling cycles
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Build the 'Capacity Sentinel & Skill-Rotor' playbook + lightweight automation to make mid-cycle scope trims and staffed buffer reallocation predictable. Goal is to reduce last-minute cross-team firefighting, increase predictability of delivery, and formalize signals that trigger fast, equitable scope cuts and role shadowing rotations.

Problem: We repeatedly face two failure modes during cycles: (1) late emergent work consumes specialized engineers and causes critical-path slippage, and (2) teams resort to manual ad-hoc borrowing which creates downstream regressions. Existing playbooks are high-level and lack a compact signal set and an automated ledger for shadow rotations and buffer consumption.

Proposed solution: A four-part approach:
1) Sentinel signals: define 6 primary metrics and thresholds (commit health, regression delta, blocker density, projected burn alignment, cross-team dependency debt, support incidents) that are evaluated each Wednesday to mark a cycle lane as 'Yellow' or 'Red'.
2) Skill-Rotor: a lightweight roster automation that recommends 0.5-1.0 FTE shadow rotations for critical skills from the shared float pool when a sentinel hits Yellow for 2 consecutive checks. Rotations are time-boxed (2 weeks) and tracked in a shared ledger.
3) Scoped trim rules: a decision matrix for automated scope downgrades tied to customer impact scoring and OKR alignment. Rules prefer deferring non-customer-visible backend improvements before trimming user-facing or security items.
4) Buffer accounting automation: a single-row ledger (Confluence table + Google Sheet) and an optional webhook that adjusts team "buffer balance" visible in the Cycle Planner dashboard.

Trade-offs & constraints:
- Automation will recommend but not enforce; PMs retain final sign-off.
- Shadow rotations reduce throughput for donor teams; the roster algorithm attempts to select low-utilization contributors first but requires manager buy-in.
- Requires integration work into Console's cycle planner and team OKR tags for reliable scoring.

Metrics for success (first 3 cycles):
- Reduce mid-cycle emergency role borrowing incidents by 60% (tracked via incident tags).
- 30% fewer unplanned scope slippages for customer-facing milestones.
- Avg time-to-decision for scope-trim reduces from 4.2 days to <24 hours when sentinel is Red.

Acceptance criteria:
- Definitions for the 6 sentinel signals documented and ratified by Eng leads + PMs.
- Skill-Rotor automation prototype that can output recommended rotations and create Linear tickets for donor teams.
- Confluence ledger and Google Sheet connected to Cycle Planner with read-only view for execs.
- Pilot run across 3 interlocking teams for cycle 2026-W12 with retrospective notes captured.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (design): finalize signals, scoring weights, and matrix (PM + Eng + Design).
- Week 2 (prototype): deliver roster recommendation script + sample ledger and integrate a webhook to create draft Linear tickets.
- Week 3 (pilot): run with 3 teams; PMs trial acceptance flow and record decisions.
- Week 4 (retro & iterate): collect metrics and refine thresholds.

Dependencies:
- cycle-planner API endpoints for per-team burn projections (ENG-50821).
- OKR tagging on work items in Console (PM-620913 - tracking ticket).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: donor team manager pushback. Mitigation: donor manager approval step on suggested rotations; allow substitution.
- Risk: false-positive Sentinels. Mitigation: require 2 consecutive checkpoints and manual PM override.

Artifacts and links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CYCLE/Capacity+Sentinel+Design+Spec
- Prototype repo (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-sentinel/prototype
- Cycle planner dashboard mock (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/XYZ/cycle-planner-sentinels

Notes on equity and fairness: the roster prioritizes volunteers, low-utilization contributors, and engineers who opted into cross-team rotations this year. We will add a visibility panel showing cumulative rotation hours by individual to ensure load balancing.

Next steps (actionable):
- PM: confirm weighting for sentinel signals by 2026-02-16 (Ava Chen).
- Eng: provide sample burn projection API by 2026-02-24 (owner: Marcus Patel).
- Design: create the visualization for Ledger & Sentinel badges by 2026-03-01 (owner: Lina Park).
